en: Spread one seat across two hearts and sit there, O Lord of hearts.
With a gracious hand keep their two hands bound in the cord of blessing.
Lord of life, may your endless love waken eternal spring in the heart,
and on the sweet union of these two souls cast your gaze of mercy.
The world's road is long and harsh; two young travellers set out upon it —
today let the sunrise of your grace reveal a new morning.
Your blessing, your greatness, your sweetness, your truth —
may these dwell in their hearts day and night, ever in new and newer forms.
O, to the nectar-sea's shore men and women have come, thirsting for sweetness.
Blessed is the night, radiant the earth;
all the world sings today in eager assurance.
In the sky your love's full moon unfolds;
sweetly blows your grace's breeze.
Waves of joy rise in the ten directions;
mind and soul are drowned in an outpouring of nectar.
O Lord, make bright this night of joy today,
unveiling the radiance of your joyful face.
Amid this gathering today, be enthroned, O King of kings;
in joy we have spread your throne.
Make beautiful, O Lord, this life and youth,
showering them with your own sweet nectar.
Take up, O take, and lay it at your feet —
this new garland of union, strung on the thread of love.
Bless, O Lord, this bond of blessing today,
bestowing your gracious benediction.
Rain down, O polestar, your blessed light-stream —
in evil days and good, remain their companion forever.
Two souls you have called and brought to one place;
over this blessed rite your gracious eye keeps watch.
With the cord of love that binds all this moving world,
bind these two in that love and keep them covered in affection's shade.
Bearing your command the two will enter the world;
by the strength of your blessing they will escape delusion's snare.
To carry out your work the two set forth today,
joining heart to heart, keeping you within their hearts.
Live in happiness, and make all others happy;
may your love be blessed in this world.
Stay always on the path of good,
keep your trust set upon greatness —
make him, the eternal Truth, your polestar in the night of doubt on the world's ocean.
May love's ever-nectared union keep life sweet;
each made strong by the other's strength, do life's work in silence.
There is much sorrow, many tears —
yet by the power of love remain unshaken.
May his will be fulfilled in danger and fortune, in grief and festival.
If the rivers of two hearts have joined into one stream,
tell us, God, toward whom does it rush so eagerly?
Before it you lie, the ocean of love;
in your infinite deep the two long to merge.
With that one hope the two have come together;
holding that one aim the two move on.
Hundreds of obstacles on the road, how many mountains of stone —
their two strengths, made one, will break them all.
And at the last, when life's great journey ends,
may they find shelter in your affection's lap;
the joy of two hearts, the sorrow of two hearts,
the hope of two hearts — may all dissolve at your feet.
Where the two meet, there you abide, Lord, you abide.
The two who walk together — you keep them, Lord, keep them with you.
Where the gaze of the two meets, there let your rain of nectar fall —
Those who call to each other — you call them, Lord, you call them.
The light the two together kindle in the lamp of their home —
in it, O God, O God of all, may your worship be offered.
Two hearts, met in sweet union, blossom on the stem of love;
from every evil you shield them, Lord, you shield them.
The boat you two have set afloat today, O new householders —
make him its helmsman who is the helmsman of this world.
He who forever, without rest, ferries all across the ocean of time —
may he send upon today's blessed voyage the stirring breeze of grace.
Take, O take your lifelong provisions; load the boat full with blessing.
In joy and sorrow, in grief, in darkness and light, go in search of the deathless.
Do not stay bound in sloth and languor; through storm and tempest go on laughing;
give your love from land to land, spreading it across the world.
On this blessed day the two have come to your feet;
teach them the lesson of love — where else would they go?
The love that never grows dull in happiness, Lord,
the love that in sorrow takes a radiant form.
The love that will stay the same forever,
that moment by moment becomes new.
The love whose white smile is a flood of morning rays,
whose tears are the dew of dawn.
The love whose path leads to the house of immortality —
show that love to these two travellers.
If ever they grow weary, take them in your lap, Merciful One —
if ever they lose the way, show it to them again.
I call out to everyone —
come, eager hearts; come, joyful souls.
Spread open your hearts; may the days and nights of this place
grant you the gift of new life.
Across sky after sky, wood after wood, and through your minds
song will be strewn and strewn again.
At the footstool of the far distance, where the lamp of blessing burns,
there you shall find your place.
Come, come, come into our courtyard, young guests, troop of trees —
take the loving company of humankind; come along, come to our home.
With green curving grace, with restless murmuring music,
bring to our door, on branch after branch, the joyous clamour of life.
On your new leaves let the sun's light dance;
give to the wind, the forest's beloved, your gift of rustling song.
Today in Shravan's downpour receive the touch of benediction;
let the streaming waters of paradise fall on your heads, on leaf after leaf.
Fly the banner of desert-conquest in the sky, O mighty life.
Bless the dust with the holiness of compassion, O tender life.
When will the song of the silent soil's heart rise murmuring in your voice —
when will sweetness fill flower, fruit and leaf, O enchanting life?
Friend of travellers, spreading a seat of shade, come, dark and beautiful one.
Come, playmate of the restless wind's games, intoxicate the blue sky.
At dawn wake on the branches the hope of song; at dusk bring words deep with rest;
at night build a nest for sleeping songs, O generous life.
O new guest, are you new, or are you eternal?
Through age after age, where were you hidden away?
With care I brought so many things and built this little house;
tell me, who invited you here?
So much hope and love, deep at the bottom of my heart,
I had kept covered in my breast, with so much laughter and tears.
Without speaking a single word you came, great queen;
how did you secretly set foot within my mind?
Come, O household deity,
make this house holy with your sacred influence.
Reign here, Mother, filling every life —
show us the ideal of a great character.
Teach us to forgive, and forgive us too;
keep your example awake in our minds;
grant patience to the heart —
a mind unshaken in joy, in sorrow, in peril.
Show night and day your stainless radiance;
bestow on the household a shining genius —
with new rays of beauty
make the home beautiful, delightful, wondrous.
Give love to all, filling every soul —
make us forget, friend, our self-pride.
all enmity will be driven away
as we welcome you, life's friend.
Come back, come back, come back to the pull of the soil —
the soil that has spread her lap-cloth and gazes at your face.
From whose bursting breast this life has risen, in whose laughter flowers have bloomed,
she who has called out in song after song.
From horizon to horizon her lap lies spread;
birth and death are strung on the unseen thread in her hand.
Her heart-melted stream of water, self-forgetful, runs toward the sea
and carries the message of life.
Come, let us reap the harvest —
reap the harvest, reap the harvest.
The field is our friend, oh, and today with its gifts
our home's courtyard will be filled day and night the whole year through.
We will take its gift — that is why we cut the paddy,
that is why we sing our song, that is why we gladly toil.
The rains came and built a magic house of shadows;
the sunshine has come, a magician of gold —
oh, that magician of gold.
Green and gold were united in the middle of our field;
that is why our beloved soil is dressed in such array.
We will take its gift — that is why we cut the paddy,
that is why we sing our song, that is why we gladly toil.
Flame of fire, come, come; bring, bring light.
In sorrow and joy, in house after house, light the household lamp.
Bring strength, bring brilliance, bring peace, bring contentment,
bring tender love, bring everlasting good.
Come along the holy path, come, O gracious one —
bring and bestow blessed sleep, blessed waking.
In the night of sorrow, in a mother's guise, keep watch unblinking;
in the festival of joy pour out your white smile.
Come, come to the festival of life,
to the flute-call of the south wind.
In the birds' morning song come, come to the holy bathing
in light's nectar-spring.
Come, come, you who are indifferent.
Come, come, you who have lost your way.
The beloved must be wed — bring, then, the bridal garland,
the offering held in your right hand.
Sorrow waits at the door —
hero, take it to your breast.
Trampling the thorns of the road, come marching, come marching
to the storm's deep cloud-thunder.
In the world-King's palace the world-vina is playing.
On land, in water, under the sky, in forest and grove,
in rivers and streams, in mountain, cave and sea,
forever wakes the fresh sweetness of music, forever the graceful play of dance.
In new spring, new joy — a new festival —
so lovely, so lovely — I hear the lovely humming in the bower;
I hear, oh I hear the murmur in the massed leaves;
in the lonely flower-grove where the koel calls.
In the midst of your tender, lovely, eye-enchanting green court
sweet melodious song is playing.
At your breath's happy touch, in overflowing delight,
the beautiful earth breaks into leaf, into bud, into hum, into rapture.
In every direction your word — ever-new your ballads — an unceasing stream of delight.
Judge my day —
at day's end I stand before you, O Lord of life.
Recalling the day's deeds, at evening I lay them at your feet —
nothing is hidden from your eyes; now pass your judgment.
If I have sunk into false observance, judge me.
If I have worshipped false gods, judge me.
If in greed I have given anyone sorrow, if in fear I have turned away from righteousness,
if I have taken pleasure in slandering others, judge me.
If I have wished evil upon anyone, judge me.
If in anger I have done anyone injustice, judge me.
The life you gave me — if I have stained it,
if I have destroyed my own self, judge me.
There is your Joy, oh,
your Joy has come there to the door — he has come, come, come, O townsfolk.
The veil from your breast, the veil of your happiness —
the veil of your sorrow — spread it in the dust, unfold it in the courtyard.
Sprinkle — all along his path, sprinkle —
wherever he sets his foot, sprinkle scented water,
so that his feet are not soiled —
your Beautiful One is there —
your Beautiful One has come there to the door — he has come, come, come.
Your heart — your yearning heart — scatter it before him,
do not hold it, do not hold it — scatter it, scatter it.
All your wealth has been made blessed, oh blessed.
For the good of all the world, today, the door of your house —
the door of your house — open it wide.
It has turned red — colour upon colour it has turned red — with the colour of whose smile?
Behold, the whole sky has turned red; the heart is drowned in rapture —
your everlasting Light has come to the door — he has come, come, come.
The lamp of your soul — lift your soul-lamp up into that light,
do not keep it, do not keep it far away —
kindle it in that light.
